# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dev-model.yaml — the single config surface for agentic-dev-kit.
#
# `init.sh` stamps your project's values here once at adoption; every kit skill
# and engine script reads this file instead of hardcoding a value. If you ever
# find yourself editing a literal inside a skill or script, that literal belongs
# here instead (Principle #10 — "No hardcoding").
#
# Run `./init.sh` to be prompted through the main values, or edit this file
# directly. NOTE: this is also the kit's OWN config, so some blocks hold this
# repo's real values rather than placeholders — each says which in its comment.
# Adopters should read every block before assuming a value is a default.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

kit:
  # Which generation of the kit's config schema this repo is on. `init.sh` stamps
  # it and migrates an older config forward in place, so re-running `./init.sh`
  # after pulling a kit update is the supported upgrade path. Never edit by hand:
  # lowering it re-runs migrations that are already applied.
  #   1 — original single-runtime schema (no `runtime:`, no `models.tiers`)
  #   2 — runtime adapters + capability tiers + engine-facing review/CI config
  version: 2

project:
  # Human-readable project name, used in skill prompts and doc headers.
  # Set for this repo. `paths:` and `doc_budgets:` below are likewise this repo's
  # own (the `kit-*.md` names, explained in the `paths:` comment); `tracker:` and
  # `notify:` are NOT — see their comments for where this repo's values live.
  name: agentic-dev-kit

paths:
  # The two canonical narrative files (Principles #1 and #2). The kit ships these
  # as docs/handoff.md and docs/friction-log.md; repoint them if your repo already
  # keeps a plan / inbox under different names.
  # THIS repo is the kit's own workspace, so its narrative files are named
  # kit-*.md. docs/handoff.md and docs/friction-log.md are the SKELETONS shipped
  # to adopters (rendered from docs/templates/ by init.sh) — if the kit pointed
  # its own plan at those, every session block would ship to adopters and the
  # unrendered marker would be gone. An adopter's own config uses the plain
  # names; only the template repo needs this indirection.
  handoff: docs/kit-handoff.md                    # the living plan / session handoff
  handoff_history: docs/kit-handoff-history.md    # swept older session blocks
  friction_log: docs/kit-friction-log.md          # the friction inbox
  friction_log_archive: docs/kit-friction-log-archive.md
  playbook: docs/autonomous-session-playbook.md   # the autonomous operating contract
  # Directory containing the deterministic kit engines. Mature repos can vendor
  # them under scripts/devkit without rewriting every workflow.
  engines: scripts

runtime:
  # Each mapping keyed by a registered launcher runtime declares its status
  # immediately above each runtime entry: `# runtime-status: mechanical` or
  # `# runtime-status: advisory`. The config-surface test discovers these maps,
  # including newly added ones; it checks declarations, not their truth.
  # Agent-specific adapters map the shared workflows onto their own command and
  # skill surfaces. `none` prints activation instructions without an agent command.
  default: claude                     # claude | codex | none | another configured key
  launchers:
    # dev_session.sh records this value and prints a copy-paste command;
    # launching it is the operator's action, not an engine-applied control.
    # runtime-status: advisory
    claude: claude
    # runtime-status: advisory
    codex: codex

parallel:
  # The supported unattended path for either runtime is one kit-owned wrapper
  # (scripts/launch_lane.py) around that runtime's stable non-interactive CLI.
  # Keep each command an argv sequence: the wrapper never invokes a shell, so a
  # launcher value cannot smuggle shell syntax into the child. A user-local
  # install (~/.local/bin, for example) is outside the wrapper's trusted lookup
  # path by design; name the absolute binary here instead.
  #
  # The three *_transport keys per runtime are DECLARATIONS the wrapper checks,
  # not free choices: it owns the vocabulary and refuses a transport the named
  # runtime does not implement. Codex: `--cd <worktree>`, prompt on stdin behind a
  # `-` argument, final text via `--output-last-message`. Claude: cwd from the
  # process, prompt on stdin, one JSON result object on stdout from
  # `--output-format json`.
  codex_headless_command: [codex, exec]
  codex_worktree_transport: cd-flag
  codex_prompt_transport: stdin-dash
  codex_final_text_transport: last-message-file
  claude_headless_command: [claude, -p]
  claude_worktree_transport: process-cwd
  claude_prompt_transport: stdin
  claude_final_text_transport: json-stdout
  # Approval/sandbox policy per runtime — a DECLARATION from the wrapper's
  # vocabulary, passed mechanically as argv. Codex: `read-only` | `workspace-write`
  # (`--sandbox <value>`; the argv is validated and passed, its behaviour is not
  # claimed until the Codex writing-lane record exists). Claude: `dont-ask` |
  # `accept-edits` (`--permission-mode dontAsk|acceptEdits`). Under `dont-ask`
  # the profile's allow list bounds every call the runtime does not accept on its
  # own: at 2.1.247 the runtime still auto-accepts a read-only Bash class (pwd,
  # whoami, cat, grep, find, bare `git remote -v` were observed live) with no
  # entry in `permission_denials`, and denies every other unlisted call. The
  # profile grants file editing through `Edit(**)`, which the runtime keeps inside
  # the worktree. `accept-edits` is declarable but NOT the default: the runtime
  # then also auto-accepts its own file-system class inside the worktree (rm, mv,
  # redirection writes were observed live) whatever the allow list says. Every
  # unrestricted spelling (bypassPermissions, danger-full-access, the
  # dangerously-* flags) is a non-member the wrapper refuses.
  codex_approval_policy: read-only
  claude_approval_policy: dont-ask
  # The Claude trust route. A freshly issued lane worktree is an untrusted
  # workspace, so the checked-out branch's `.claude/settings.json` never supplies
  # policy (its allow list is ignored there and its hooks would otherwise still
  # run) and the operator's user settings must not either. The wrapper passes
  # `--setting-sources ""` plus this cockpit-owned profile through `--settings`;
  # it is the ONE settings source a lane loads. Path relative to the repo root or
  # absolute; seeded by init.sh when absent and adopter-owned afterwards. The
  # wrapper refuses a profile whose `permissions` object carries any key other
  # than `allow`, `deny`, `ask` (`defaultMode`, `additionalDirectories`, an
  # unrecognised key) or a whole-tool Bash allowance.
  claude_settings_profile: config/claude-lane-settings.json
  # A descriptor is a one-shot launch authority, not standing permission. The
  # issuer stamps this lifetime into the descriptor and the wrapper rejects an
  # expired value before starting a child.
  descriptor_ttl_seconds: 900
  # The parent waits only this long for the child-side Git/filesystem/process
  # observation to become durable before refusing the launch.
  observation_timeout_seconds: 30
  # An interrupted or rejected launch gets this bounded graceful-stop window
  # before the wrapper escalates to forced process-group termination.
  termination_grace_seconds: 5

doc_budgets:
  # Line-count tripwires (the archival mechanism of Principle #1). A file over budget
  # is a housekeeping nudge: check_doc_budget.py exits 0 by default even when one is
  # over, and returns 1 only under --strict. It exits 2 on a usage or CONFIG error
  # regardless of flags — including a `path:` here that no longer exists — so a renamed
  # doc gates any pipeline running it, however it is invoked.
  - path: docs/kit-handoff.md
    budget: 400
    archive: docs/kit-handoff-history.md
    # This budget is in LINES; archive_plan_sessions.py's --keep is in BLOCKS, so
    # --keep at its default can be a no-op against this budget (issue #74: 5 blocks
    # under --keep 6 while still over on lines). --target-lines closes that gap by
    # sweeping to a line count directly — name it here, not --keep.
    # `{budget}` is substituted by check_doc_budget.py from the `budget:` above.
    # Write the placeholder, never the literal: a restated number goes stale the
    # moment the budget moves, and the warning would then prescribe the old target.
    remedy: "run the wrap-up workflow to sweep old session blocks into the history file (archive_plan_sessions.py --target-lines {budget}, not --keep — this budget is in lines, not blocks)"
  - path: docs/kit-friction-log.md
    budget: 150
    archive: docs/kit-friction-log-archive.md
    remedy: "run the triage-friction-log workflow to graduate the inbox to the tracker"

vcs:
  forge: github                  # github | gitlab | other — some skills branch on this
  protected_branch: main         # never committed to directly; PRs target this
  # Prefix for ISOLATED LANE branches (<prefix>/<scope>) — not for cockpit work.
  # scripts/hooks/pre-push refuses a push from <prefix>/* that touches the narrative
  # files. Cockpit branches are anything outside that prefix — chore/*, feat/*, a
  # hand-named PR branch; the hook skips them all, it does not require a name.
  dev_branch_prefix: dev
  # {date} expands to today's ISO date at skill runtime.
  triage_branch_pattern: "chore/triage-{date}"
  systemize_branch_pattern: "chore/systemize-{date}"

triage:
  # Shared triage-friction-log workflow settings. Runtime adapters translate
  # invocation and available mechanisms only; approval and write policy stays in
  # the shared workflow.
  analysis_tier: default
  # Live and test approval sessions never share state. Frozen inputs and reports
  # also carry a generated session id so a later same-day run cannot replace the
  # evidence an earlier approval bound.
  state_path: "state/triage/triage-pipeline-state_{mode}.json"
  # The single-writer gate is a separate, mode-specific logical state path.
  # Resolve it through state_paths exactly like state_path; never derive or
  # hardcode a worktree-local lock location.
  gate_path: "state/triage/triage-pipeline-gate_{mode}.lock"
  # Deterministic recovery evidence locator. gate_digest is SHA-256 over the
  # exact complete gate bytes, so a crash-resuming invocation never scans for
  # a matching bundle or confuses it with another gate's evidence.
  recovery_bundle_pattern: "state/triage/recovery-bundle_{mode}_{gate_digest}.json"
  frozen_inbox_pattern: "state/triage/frozen-inbox_{mode}_{date}_{session}.json"
  report_root: reports
  report_pattern: "reports/triage_{mode}_{date}_{session}.md"
  # Optional deterministic integration, resolved beneath paths.engines. Both
  # present selects engine-backed mode, both absent selects honest LLM-only mode,
  # and a partial pair is a configuration failure.
  draft_engine: triage_friction_log.py
  finalize_engine: finalize_triage.py
  commit_subject: "docs(triage): graduate friction-log entries"
  # This workflow completes its patch before PR creation, so false is the only
  # valid value. True hard-stops instead of manufacturing a draft window.
  pr_draft: false

systemize:
  # Shared post-merge-systemize workflow settings. The runtime adapter selects
  # no policy: Claude and Codex both read this block and the shared workflow.
  analysis_tier: expensive
  # Exact forge logins trusted as operator review-finding sources. Empty is the
  # adopter-safe default; ./init.sh prompts rather than trusting a foreign identity.
  operator_logins: []
  lookback_days: 7
  backfill_days: 28
  pattern_threshold: 2
  tracker_severity: high
  batch_size: 25
  single_pass_max_prs: 60
  max_findings_prs_per_run: 75
  # {window} is the selected lookback in days (for example 7d); {mode} is
  # live or test. Together they keep same-day entry points from sharing state.
  cache_pattern: "state/cache/merged-prs_{window}_{mode}_{date}.json"
  digest_cache_pattern: "state/cache/merged-prs-digest_{window}_{mode}_{date}.json"
  # Separate trusted root lets preflight reject a mistaken report_pattern that
  # points at source or config while keeping the filename configurable.
  report_root: reports
  report_pattern: "reports/post-merge-systemize_{window}_{mode}_{date}.md"
  # Optional deterministic integration, resolved beneath paths.engines. The
  # shipped kit does not vendor these yet: all absent selects the documented
  # LLM-only path, all present selects engine-backed mode, and a partial set
  # stops rather than mixing incompatible artifacts.
  fetch_engine: fetch_merged_prs.py
  digest_engine: digest_merged_prs.py
  heartbeat_engine: heartbeat_cli.py
  commit_subject: "docs(systemize): promote recurring review patterns"
  # This workflow completes its patch before PR creation, so false is the only
  # valid value. True hard-stops instead of manufacturing a draft window. The
  # workflow never merges the PR; pr-watch supplies review follow-through and
  # the operator decides.
  pr_draft: false

tracker:
  # This repo's real values, not placeholders. ADOPTERS: replace all three.
  # `init.sh` prompts with these as defaults and refuses, on a non-interactive run,
  # to keep a project_name that does not match your origin remote.
  backend: github-issues         # linear | github-issues | jira | none
  project_name: "topij/agentic-dev-kit"
  url: "https://github.com/topij/agentic-dev-kit/issues"
  # Linear-only ids. Kept blank rather than removed: `init.sh` writes into this
  # sub-map when an adopter selects `linear`, and only rewrites existing lines.
  linear:
    team_id: ""
    project_id: ""
    label_name: ""
review:
  # Independent review present on this repo (Principle #5). A down bot is not a
  # review waiver; select the current runtime's substitute pass instead.
  # Also read by pr_watch.py to identify which status checks and comment authors
  # belong to a reviewer, so its outage/pending state can reach the merge gate.
  # Matched case-insensitively: as a SUBSTRING of a check name (your own CI and
  # bot config, so `Review / CodeRabbit` still matches), and as the exact
  # normalized login of a comment author plus explicitly trusted service aliases
  # (`coderabbit` covers `coderabbitai` and `coderabbitai[bot]`). Anyone may
  # comment on a public PR, so prefix matching would let a lookalike login speak
  # for the reviewer. Keep entries specific enough not to collide with a CI job
  # name.
  bots: [coderabbit]
  # Exact GitHub logins trusted to speak for each configured reviewer. Keep
  # aliases explicit: prefix inference lets a lookalike account impersonate a
  # reviewer. Custom bots whose check name and author login differ belong here.
  bot_author_aliases:
    coderabbit: [coderabbitai, "coderabbitai[bot]"]
  # Extra CREATOR identities trusted to announce an OUTAGE for a bot (#95).
  #
  # A check's NAME is chosen by whoever created the check, and on a same-repo PR
  # that can be the PR's own workflow (`checks: write` / `statuses: write`). A
  # check called `coderabbit-shim` whose description matched an
  # `unavailable_markers` entry used to cancel the real reviewer's pending block
  # and open the merge gate mid-review. So the CANCEL now requires the creator
  # identity GitHub records — `app.slug` on a check run, `creator.login` on a
  # status context — which a workflow cannot forge: its GITHUB_TOKEN
  # authenticates as `github-actions`, never as the reviewer's app. The outage is
  # still REPORTED either way, so the signal to run the fallback panel survives.
  #
  # Ordinarily leave this empty. pr_watch already derives the common case from
  # `bot_author_aliases` above, since an app's slug and its `<slug>[bot]` login
  # are conventionally the same string — verified on this repo, whose real
  # CodeRabbit status contexts carry `creator.login: coderabbitai[bot]` while the
  # aliases already list `coderabbitai`. Set it only for a bot whose app slug
  # genuinely differs from the login it comments under.
  #
  # Same "enumerate, never infer" rule as the aliases: entries are matched
  # EXACTLY, never as a prefix or substring. A prefix rule here would let
  # `coderabbit-impersonator` announce CodeRabbit's outage, which is the defect
  # this key exists to close, one namespace over.
  #
  # Left ABSENT rather than written as an empty `{}`: the kit's own config reader
  # (`scripts/lib/kitconfig`) supports flow SEQUENCES but not flow MAPPINGS, so
  # `bot_app_slugs: {}` parses to the *string* `"{}"` there while PyYAML reads an
  # empty dict — the two disagree, which `test_matches_pyyaml_on_the_shipped_config`
  # catches. An absent key takes the same built-in empty default. When you do need
  # it, write it in block form, which both parsers agree on:
  #
  #   bot_app_slugs:
  #     coderabbit: [some-other-app-slug]
  # The independent pass to run when a configured bot can't review. TWO shapes,
  # and the difference is whether the reviewer is independent of the author:
  #
  #   fallback_panel     one isolated, fresh-context reviewer PER LENS. This is
  #                      the real substitute — `safety-critical-changes.md`
  #                      rule 2 wants two disjoint lenses, which a single
  #                      command cannot be.
  #   fallback_commands  one command in the cockpit's own context. When the
  #                      cockpit authored the diff that is the author
  #                      re-reading their own work — kept as the DEGRADED mode
  #                      for a runtime with no way to isolate a reviewer.
  #
  # Which lenses is adopter knowledge and lives here; how a lens must be run
  # (fresh context, raw diff, no author framing, execute rather than only read,
  # mutation-test new branches) is kit doctrine and lives in
  # docs/agentic-dev-kit/fallback-review-panel.md.
  #
  # Three receipt literals exist, one per pass: `fallback:panel` (the
  # receipt_source below), `fallback:<runtime>` (the Degraded-mode
  # author-context run of fallback_commands — e.g. `fallback:claude`), and
  # `fallback:delta` (the record-prose delta pass defined in that doctrine
  # file's stopping section — one lens ordinarily, both lenses for a change
  # under safety-critical-changes.md; `--lenses` records which form ran).
  # The last two are literals the recording agent writes on the receipt, not
  # config keys — never set receipt_source to either.
  #
  # A FOURTH literal exists and is not a fallback pass at all:
  # `<bot>:comment-verdict` (#44), for a reviewer that announced a clean review
  # in a comment and created no review object, so the gate cannot see it. It
  # takes no `--lenses` because no lens ran, and it is deliberately outside the
  # `fallback:` namespace — those stand for a substitute review, and this one
  # stands for the real reviewer on a surface the gate cannot read. Also never a
  # receipt_source. See `comment_verdict_markers` below and the
  # "When the reviewer answered and the gate cannot see it" section of
  # docs/agentic-dev-kit/fallback-review-panel.md.
  fallback_panel:
    receipt_source: "fallback:panel"   # never the same as a single-lens receipt
    # Compute for each panel lens, keyed by runtime — the same per-runtime shape
    # `models.runtime_mappings` uses, because the panel runs under whichever
    # runtime the cockpit is.
    #
    # `model` selects the model, `effort` the reasoning level. BOTH ARE OPTIONAL
    # and independent: set either, both, or neither. A runtime exposing only one
    # control carries only that key; omitting a runtime entirely means its lenses
    # inherit the cockpit session's own compute, which is the pre-existing
    # behaviour and stays the default for anyone who does not set this.
    #
    # HOW FAR EACH KEY REACHES is declared per runtime, from live probes of the
    # pinned clients (Claude Code 2.1.247 and codex-cli 0.149.1 on 2026-08-27;
    # saved_plans/capability-tier-calibration-live-validation_2026-08-27.md is
    # the record, with the commands and the observer fields):
    #
    #   claude.model   MECHANICAL — the cockpit passes it as the delegation
    #                  tool's `model` parameter, or the kit-owned agent
    #                  definition `.claude/agents/<lens>.md` carries it; the
    #                  runtime applies it and the session transcript reads the
    #                  resolved model id back. The tool's parameter overrides the
    #                  definition's value.
    #   claude.effort  MECHANICAL through the agent definition only. The
    #                  delegation tool has no effort parameter, so a lens launched
    #                  as a plain subagent inherits the cockpit's effort and this
    #                  key is ADVISORY there (prompt text). Launch the agent named
    #                  after the lens; `scripts/panel_prompt.py --agent-definition`
    #                  renders it from this block and refuses a level the runtime
    #                  would silently drop (an invalid frontmatter effort is logged
    #                  only under --debug and runs at the parent's effort).
    #   codex.effort   MECHANICAL — passed as `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>`
    #                  on the `codex exec` argv and read back from the rollout's
    #                  `turn_context`. A misspelled `-c` KEY is accepted silently
    #                  at the config default (exit 0), so copy the key exactly; an
    #                  invalid LEVEL is refused by the API (exit 1).
    #   codex.model    MECHANICAL when set (`-m <model>`); absent here on purpose,
    #                  so a lens runs the model in the user's Codex config, which
    #                  is the one their account is known to have.
    #
    # The `Run at:` line panel_prompt.py renders into a prompt restates these and
    # enforces nothing on either runtime; it names the carrier beside the value.
    #
    # Why sonnet rather than the `expensive` tier: measured 2026-08-01 over two
    # real panels on this repo — a docs PR (~196k output tokens) and a code PR
    # (~167k). Both produced findings the cockpit had missed, including a stale
    # verified-output claim and a root-container run the cockpit had declared
    # impossible. Lens work is bounded and adversarial rather than open-ended, so
    # it does not need the judgment tier; `effort: high` is what carries it.
    # Re-measure before assuming this holds for your repo — cost tracked CLAIM
    # DENSITY, not code complexity, and the docs PR was the expensive one.
    lens_compute:
      # Mechanical through the agent definition; plain-subagent effort is
      # advisory, as the per-control carrier declaration above explains.
      # runtime-status: mechanical
      claude:
        model: sonnet
        effort: high
      # runtime-status: mechanical
      codex:
        effort: high
    lenses:
      - name: adversarial
        focus: "assume the change is wrong and try to prove it — bypasses, fail-open paths, wedges, and whether the new guard actually guards"
      - name: correctness
        focus: "assume it works and ask what it says — stale comments, claims that overstate what is verified, tests whose names promise more than their bodies check"
  fallback_commands:
    # pr_followup_hook.py renders a reminder; the agent must run the command.
    # runtime-status: advisory
    claude: "/code-review"
    # runtime-status: advisory
    codex: "/review"
  # Everything below is read by scripts/pr_watch.py. It used to live as literals
  # inside that engine, which meant adopting the kit required *editing the
  # engine* — and an edited engine can never be replaced by a kit update. Keeping
  # it here is what makes engines kit-owned and upgradable (Principle #10).
  #
  # Comment bodies matching any of these are auto-noise, not findings to act on.
  # Matched case-insensitively as substrings. Keep the list tight — over-filtering
  # hides a real review. `is_noise()` does NOT check the author, so every entry
  # here also discards a HUMAN comment that happens to contain the text: prefer a
  # structural marker (an HTML comment the bot emits) over the bot's prose.
  #
  # `"actionable comments posted: 0"` used to sit here and was retired under
  # #468. A sweep of every comment body on every PR this repo has ever had found
  # it matched nothing, ever: CodeRabbit writes "Actionable comments posted: N"
  # only on the review-submission surface and only when N >= 1, and delivers the
  # zero case as a sentence inside the summary comment instead. That sentence is
  # deliberately NOT added in its place — see
  # `test_a_human_quoting_the_clean_verdict_is_not_noise` in
  # scripts/tests/test_pr_watch.py, which is the tripwire against re-adding it.
  noise_markers:
    - "<!-- this is an auto-generated comment: summarize by coderabbit"
    - "<!-- this is an auto-generated comment: review in progress"
    - "<!-- walkthrough_start -->"
    - "<!-- linear-linkback -->"
  # Text signalling the reviewer could not run — a blocked bot is an action
  # signal (run the configured fallback), never a silent review waiver. Matched
  # against two surfaces, which behave differently on purpose:
  #   - a COMMENT body: deliberately not noise, so it surfaces as a new comment
  #     and blocks `converged` until acknowledged.
  #   - a configured bot's STATUS-CHECK description: surfaced and reported, but
  #     blocks nothing — there is no comment to acknowledge, so blocking on it
  #     would wedge the loop. It is the surface that carried the outage on #22
  #     and made a rate-limited bot read as a clean review (issue #23).
  # The same outage is worded differently on each, which is why matching only
  # comments made detection depend on which one the bot happened to use.
  unavailable_markers:
    - "bugbot needs on-demand usage enabled"
    - "review limit reached"
    - "rate limited by coderabbit"
    - "review rate limited"       # the status-check wording of "review limit reached"
    - "couldn't start this review"
    - "review skipped"
    - "no review credits"
  # Text in a configured bot's COMMENT that announces a COMPLETED review (#44).
  #
  # Some reviewers deliver a clean verdict as an issue comment and create no
  # review object, so `review_bots.coverage` — which reads review objects — sees
  # nothing, and a PR that WAS independently reviewed is indistinguishable from
  # one that never was. Measured on this repo: whether a review object exists
  # tracks whether the review found anything, so the clean pass is exactly the
  # one the merge gate cannot see.
  #
  # What these markers do is REPORT that, as `review_bots.comment_verdicts`.
  # They do NOT satisfy the merge gate. That is the ruling on #44 (2026-08-17)
  # and the reason this key is safe to key on prose at all: the failure of a
  # marker that stops matching is a missing report line, never an authorized
  # merge. `bot_review_coverage`'s docstring is the standing argument for why
  # the other direction is not available — treating a comment-shaped verdict as
  # coverage would authorize merges on a prose match.
  #
  # Matched case-insensitively as substrings, and ONLY as one term of a
  # conjunction (see `bot_comment_verdicts`): the comment must also CONTAIN the
  # current head — a bare case-insensitive substring test, with no length, hex,
  # or word-boundary condition — and must NOT match any `unavailable_markers`
  # entry. This used to say "must carry the current head's full SHA", which
  # described the caller rather than the check: every production caller passes
  # `headRefOid`, but nothing in the matching logic verifies it (#536).
  # That last term is not decoration — on #263 a rate-limited bot posted a
  # comment naming the commit range it WOULD have reviewed, so a rule keyed on
  # the SHA alone would have manufactured evidence for a review that never ran.
  #
  # `actionable comments posted:` is deliberately open-ended — it matches
  # `N >= 1` too. A review that found things is still a review that happened,
  # and its findings arrive through `new_comments` regardless.
  comment_verdict_markers:
    - "no actionable comments were generated"
    - "actionable comments posted:"
  # Status checks that are advisory only and must never block `converged` — this
  # is the anti-wedge property: a review bot's check can sit PENDING forever after
  # a trivial follow-up commit, and the watch loop must still be able to finish.
  # Its real findings arrive as comments (which DO block). Matched
  # case-insensitively against the check name.
  #
  # Note the deliberate overlap with `bots` above: SAME value, DIFFERENT purpose.
  # This list is a blocking policy ("this check never blocks the watch loop");
  # `bots` is an identity ("this check belongs to a reviewer whose state the
  # merge gate cares about"). Splitting them is what lets a bot's check stay
  # non-blocking for `converged` while its pending/unavailable state still
  # reaches `mergeable`.
  informational_checks: [coderabbit]
  # How long a configured review bot's own check may sit pending before the merge
  # gate stops waiting for it. BELOW this, a pending bot blocks `mergeable`: a
  # review is genuinely coming, and a receipt recorded now would bind to a review
  # that has not happened (issue #19 — a receipt taken against a merely queued
  # bot let four valid findings land post-merge). ABOVE it, the bot is treated as
  # never going to report and stops blocking, which is what keeps a dead bot from
  # wedging the merge gate. Never affects `converged`.
  bot_pending_grace_minutes: 15
  # How long the check rollup must STOP CHANGING SIZE, for the
  # current head, before the
  # merge gate believes it is complete. Guards the two routes by which a partial
  # rollup used to read as a finished one (issues #190 and #39): a lost or
  # first-run state file, which leaves no baseline to compare against — a fresh
  # clone reaches that with no failed write anywhere — and a head change, which
  # rebaselines to the new commit's PARTIAL count so the next poll compares it
  # against itself. Neither is detectable from a count: the rollup never says how
  # many checks are still coming, so 2-of-5 and 2-of-2 are the same number.
  #
  # The clock runs from when the rollup last MOVED, not from the push, so it
  # elapses concurrently with CI rather than after it — on a repo whose checks
  # take longer than this to finish, it adds no merge latency at all. Blocks
  # `mergeable` only, NEVER `converged`: the watch loop must stay runnable.
  #
  # 0 drops the time requirement but still requires a baseline to exist, so a
  # fresh clone blocks for the single poll it takes to record one. Re-measure
  # against your own CI's check-registration spread before tuning; this repo runs
  # one check, so it has no spread to measure.
  #
  # IF YOU SET `require_ci: false` ABOVE, read this. Your rollup is permanently
  # empty, so this guard buys you nothing and still costs one extra poll plus the
  # grace before a merge. `0` is the setting for you: it keeps the one-poll
  # baseline (so a lost state file still cannot authorize a merge) and drops the
  # wait. The engine deliberately does NOT skip the guard on an empty rollup by
  # itself — a first poll looks identical whether there are no checks or the
  # checks have not registered yet, and guessing there is the fail-open the guard
  # exists to prevent.
  settle_grace_minutes: 3
  # Whether a PR must have at least one real (non-informational) CI check before
  # pr_watch will report green. True is the safe default: it stops an autonomous
  # merge on a PR whose CI never ran. Set false for a repo with no CI at all —
  # otherwise pr-watch can never converge and `dev_session.sh merge` always
  # refuses. With false, `mergeable` still requires current-head independent-review
  # EVIDENCE — either a recorded receipt or a configured bot's own review of that
  # head (#350) — and that evidence becomes the only quality gate, so set this
  # deliberately. Note what the two settings compose into: `require_ci: false` on a
  # repo with `bots: []` leaves the receipt as the single gate, since the
  # bot-coverage route needs a configured bot to exist.
  require_ci: true

notify:
  backend: slack                 # slack | none — where skills DM the operator
  # Blank ON PURPOSE. This is an identity: put it in the gitignored
  # `config/dev-model.local.yaml`, which is merged over this file. See
  # docs/getting-started.md.
  user_key: ""
models:
  # Runtime-neutral capability tiers (Principle #7). Workflows assign a tier; an
  # adapter may translate it to a model, effort level, or leave it as guidance when
  # the runtime cannot select compute per delegated task.
  tiers:
    cheap: mechanical
    default: standard
    expensive: judgment
  # STATUS, per runtime: ADVISORY on both. No engine reads this map:
  # `grep -rn runtime_mappings scripts/ init.sh` finds init.sh's migration write
  # and test pins, never an engine (read at 16b07d6 and re-read at e128cdc, where
  # this PR's own tests had joined the pins — the panel's correctness lens caught
  # two earlier versions of this parenthetical enumerating too few files, which
  # is why it now names the kinds and not the files). So a workflow's tier
  # reaches a session only when the
  # cockpit or the operator applies the value by hand — the delegation tool's
  # `model` parameter, `claude -p --model/--effort`, `codex -m` and
  # `-c model_reasoning_effort=`. The VALUES below name controls each client was
  # observed to accept (Claude Code 2.1.247, codex-cli 0.149.1, 2026-08-27;
  # saved_plans/capability-tier-calibration-live-validation_2026-08-27.md):
  #
  #   claude — model aliases the client resolved and reported back in the
  #            result's `modelUsage`: haiku, sonnet, opus, fable. A model the
  #            account lacks fails at exit 1 naming it, so an account without
  #            `fable` sets `expensive: opus` here. Effort is inherited unless a
  #            `.claude/agents/*.md` definition or `--effort` sets it; `--effort`
  #            with an unknown level WARNS on stderr and runs at the default.
  #   codex  — reasoning-effort levels `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` applied
  #            and read back from the rollout: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, and
  #            none; `minimal` was refused by the API for the probed model. The
  #            model is inherited from the user's Codex config unless `-m` is
  #            passed; a model the account lacks fails at exit 1.
  #
  # `expensive` points at the top of what each client exposed on that date:
  # `fable` resolved to the runtime's latest top model, and `xhigh` is the
  # highest Codex level short of `max`. Claude's judgment tier moves the MODEL
  # and inherits effort; Codex's moves EFFORT on the user's model. Parity is the
  # tier outcome, not the same knob.
  #
  # A tier's value may be EITHER a scalar or a `{model, effort}` map.
  #
  # The scalar form is the original and stays valid — it means "the one compute
  # control this runtime exposes", which is why the two runtimes below
  # read as different things: `claude` names models, `codex` names effort levels.
  # That ambiguity is the reason the map form exists. Prefer it when a runtime
  # exposes both controls and you want to pin them independently — both clients
  # accept the same effort spellings low, medium, high, xhigh, max, so a map's
  # `effort` reads the same under either:
  #
  #   claude:
  #     expensive: { model: fable, effort: high }
  #     cheap:     { effort: low }          # model inherited
  #
  # Either key may be omitted; an omitted key inherits the session's own value.
  # Kept as scalars here because that is what this repo actually uses — see
  # `review.fallback_panel.lens_compute` for the map form in live use.
  runtime_mappings:
    # runtime-status: advisory
    claude:
      cheap: haiku
      default: sonnet
      expensive: fable
    # runtime-status: advisory
    codex:
      cheap: low
      default: medium
      expensive: xhigh

state:
  # The per-lane state sandbox (Principle #3) is driven by FIXED, project-neutral env
  # vars (DEVKIT_STATE_ROOT / DEVKIT_ROOT) and a `.devkit_state_root` marker file —
  # see scripts/lib/state_paths/. Those are kit constants, not adopter config; listed
  # here only so the convention is discoverable. `dirname` is the top-level state dir.
  dirname: state
  # The unsandboxed-write guard skips a legitimate scheduled/CI writer, detected by
  # env var. state_paths stays import-free (it must work from a git hook), so this is
  # an ENV contract, not a value it reads from here — documented here for
  # discoverability only:
  #   DEVKIT_CI_ENV_VARS  comma-separated var names whose presence means "cron/CI".
  #                       Default: JOB_NAME,CI,GITHUB_ACTIONS,GITLAB_CI,BUILDKITE
  # Set it in your runner if your scheduler exports something else.
